Mechanistic Modulation of Protein Amyloid Aggregation by Metal-Containing and Amino Acid-Based Ionic Liquids

Abstract:

Protein misfolding and abnormal aggregation are fundamental processes involved in neurodegenerative and systemic amyloid diseases. Soluble oligomers and insoluble amyloid fibrils can also cause protein disruption and dysfunction, leading to cellular dysfunction and toxicity. &nbspHence, understanding and controlling protein aggregation is crucial to protein science, its stabilization and functional biomolecular systems. The tunable physicochemical properties and specific biomolecular interactions of ionic liquids (ILs) have made them promising modulators of protein stability, folding, and aggregation. Magnetic ionic liquids (MILs) are liquids that contain paramagnetic metal ions, which offer another platform to explore the role of metal centres in protein aggregation. The goal of this research is to create strategies for controlling protein aggregation in ILs, first by applying the well-established model of the lysozyme protein. The synthesis and characterization of an iron based MIL was carried out and the inhibitory effect on lysozyme aggregation was confirmed by ThT, ANS, CD spectroscopy and confocal imaging. Additional techniques, such as FTIR and TEM, will be employed to validate the findings and provide further insights into conformational changes, hydrophobic exposure, &beta-sheet formation, aggregate growth, and fibril development. Various metal centres, amino-acid based ILs and other proteins like BMP-2 will then be studied. Finally, the controlled aggregation of proteins will be investigated for the creation of aggregated protein biomaterials.
